'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[National Society of Film Critics]] names [[Contemporary Western|contemporary western]] film ''[[Nomadland (film)|Nomadland]]'' as the recipient of 2020's [[National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Film]]. [https://www.thewrap.com/nomadland-named-best-film-by-national-society-of-film-critics/ (''The Wrap'')]
*Thousands of [[Roman Catholic]] devotees attend Saturday masses organized in lieu of the cancelled annual procession of the [[Black Nazarene]] at the [[Quiapo Church]] in [[Manila]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-religion-philippines/philippines-catholics-display-devotion-to-christ-statue-pray-for-end-of-pandemic-idUSL4N2JK00A (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182]]
**[[Indonesia]]n authorities lose contact with [[Sriwijaya Air]] Flight 182 shortly after take-off with 62 people onboard. The [[passenger plane]], a [[Boeing 737]], was en route to [[Pontianak]], taking off from the [[capital city|capital]] [[Jakarta]]. [https://www.theage.com.au/world/asia/authorities-lose-contact-with-boeing-737-flight-over-indonesia-20210109-p56swv.html (''The Age'')]
*[[2020–21 European windstorm season]]
**[[Storm Filomena]] causes the death of two people from heavy rains in the [[province of Málaga]] and another two from [[hypothermia]] after a [[blizzard]] hits central [[Spain]]. The [[Mayor of Madrid]] requests the assistance of the [[Spanish Army|Army]] as he considers the situation in the capital to be of "extreme gravity". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-55586751 (BBC News)] [https://www.europapress.es/madrid/noticia-almeida-avisa-situacion-extrema-gravedad-pide-madrilenos-no-salgan-casas-20210109110142.html (Europa Press)]
*Ten newborn babies die in a hospital fire in western [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. The fire was supposedly caused by an electrical [[short circuit]]. [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] says that the news was "heart-wrenching". [https://www.dw.com/en/india-10-newborn-babies-killed-in-hospital-blaze/a-56177825 (DW)]
*A nationwide [[Power outage|blackout]] occurs in [[Pakistan]], leaving more than 200 million people without power. [[Senate of Pakistan|Senator]] [[Faisal Javed Khan]] says that the blackout was apparently caused by a "sudden frequency drop in the power transmission system". Power is gradually being restored in some parts of the country. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2021/01/pakistan-hit-by-nationwide-blackout/ (BNO News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[California]] reports a record 695 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the cumulative death toll in the state to 29,233. [https://ktla.com/news/local-news/california-reports-record-695-covid-19-deaths-in-1-day/ (KTLA-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Minnesota]] reports its first five cases of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated from the [[United Kingdom]]. The patients are aged 15 to 37. [https://www.kare11.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/mn-reports-5-cases-of-new-covid-strain-originally-found-in-uk/89-3e868858-30d4-4e65-a26d-8995e8b4e969 (KARE-TV)]
****The United States surpasses 22 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/u-s-covid-19-cases-hit-22-million-scientists-track-n1253643 (NBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
*****A nighttime curfew takes effect in [[Quebec]] in an effort to contain the spread of COVID-19. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/nightly-curfew-pandemic-takes-effect-quebec-75157351 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] reports a record 16,105 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,524,036. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mexico/mexico-hits-daily-covid-19-record-with-16105-new-cases-health-ministry-idUSKBN29F00S (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom]]
*****Queen [[Elizabeth II]] and [[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]] receive their first doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/royal-family/2021/01/09/queen-has-given-coronavirus-vaccine-palace-announces/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
****The [[United Kingdom]] surpasses 80,000 deaths and 3 million cases of COVID-19, becoming the fifth country to do so after the [[United States]], [[Brazil]], [[India]], and [[Russia]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55605173 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/09/uk-covid-deaths-pass-80000-and-confirmed-cases-pass-3m (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****[[Pope Francis]] confirms in an interview with Italian broadcaster [[Canale 5]] that the vaccination campaign in [[Vatican City]] will begin next week and that he will receive the vaccine. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/01/09/europe/pope-covid-vaccine-intl-scli/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.euronews.com/2021/01/09/pope-francis-has-appointment-to-be-vaccinated-against-covid-19-next-week (Euronews)]
****[[Fabrizio Soccorsi]], Pope Francis' personal physician, dies as a result of "complications due to COVID-19", according to Vatican newspaper ''[[L'Osservatore Romano]]''. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/pope-francis-personal-doctor-coronavirus (Fox News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[France]] extends its curfew to eight [[Departments of France|departments]], including [[Bouches-du-Rhône]], which includes [[Marseille]], where a 6:00 p.m. curfew has been imposed after 21 people tested positive for the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210109-france-extends-6pm-curfew-to-marseille-as-21-test-positive-for-uk-variant (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[Government of the People's Republic of China|Chinese authorities]] tell 16 million residents in [[Shijiazhuang]] and [[Xingtai]] to stay home for the next seven days as Shijiazhuang suspends all public transport in order to combat the new outbreak of [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/9/china-tightens-restrictions-in-two-cities-south-of-beijing (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****The [[Government of India|government]] announces that [[India]] will begin its [[COVID-19 vaccination]] campaign on January 16 with priority given to an estimated 30 million [[healthcare worker|healthcare]] and frontline workers. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/india-to-start-covid-19-vaccination-drive-on-jan-16/article33536670.ece (''The Hindu'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] becomes the first [[Israel]]i to get a second dose of [[Pfizer]]'s [[tozinameran]] vaccine as the country begins administering second doses of the vaccine to the public. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-launches-2nd-dose-drive-as-serious-covid-cases-hit-record-high-of-964/ (''The Times of Israel'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] surpasses 4,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/01/09/national/japan-jan9-coronavirus/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] surpasses 10,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2048163/212-new-covid-cases-187-local (''Bangkok Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Taiwan–United States relations]]
**Outgoing [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces that the United States will be lifting all restrictions on contacts between American and [[Taiwan]]ese officials, saying the "self-imposed" restrictions were introduced decades ago to appease the [[Chinese Communist Party]] government in [[mainland China]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-55606594 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
***The [[United States Attorney for the District of Columbia]] announces that [[Jacob Chansley]] (also known as [[Jake Angeli]] or "[[QAnon]] [[shaman]]"), who was photographed wearing horns during the [[United States Capitol|Capitol]] [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|riot]], has been arrested. Additionally, Adam Christian Johnson is also expected to face charges for carrying [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]]'s [[lectern]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/09/capitol-pelosi-lectern-police-arrest-adam-christian-johnson (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.tmz.com/2021/01/09/man-horn-hat-flag-paint-capitol-arrested-fbi-jacob-chansley/ (TMZ)]
***[[West Virginia House of Delegates|West Virginia delegate]] [[Derrick Evans (politician)|Derrick Evans]] resigns a day after being arrested for illegally entering the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://wvmetronews.com/2021/01/09/derrick-evans-resigns-w-va-house-after-entering-u-s-capitol-with-mob/ (''West Virginia MetroNews'')]
**Virginia Governor [[Ralph Northam]] announces that detachments of the [[Virginia National Guard]] and [[Virginia State Police]] will remain stationed at the [[United States Capitol]] through the [[inauguration of Joe Biden]] on January 20. [https://www.nbc12.com/2021/01/07/governor-northam-orders-vsp-national-guard-remain-washington/ (WWBT-TV)]
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**Three people are killed and four others injured in a [[shooting spree]] through several neighborhoods in the [[South Side, Chicago|South Side]] area of [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], as well as [[Evanston, Illinois|Evanston]]. The shooter, a 32-year-old man, was shot during a [[shootout]] with responding Evanston police officers and later died in a hospital. [https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/evanston-police-fatally-shoot-suspect-who-killed-5-during-shooting-spree/2412658/ (WMAQ-TV)]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[Parler]] app is suspended indefinitely from the [[App Store]] by [[Apple Inc.]] Additionally, [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] also announces that they will discontinue providing cloud services for Parler due to incitement of violence, which will go into effect on Sunday at 11:59 p.m. Pacific time. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/09/tech/parler-suspended-apple-app-store/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/09/amazon-drops-parler-from-its-web-hosting-service.html (CNBC)]
